Abstract.AbstractText: Immunoglobulin E (IgE) gammopathy is a rare disorder, accounting for just 0.1% of all patients with multiple myeloma (MM). Herein, we report a case of IgE monoclonal gammopathy without any biological and clinical symptoms, and we review 63 published cases in the literature. Demographic, biological and clinical presentations and features appear to be similar to those of other subtypes of MM, with a median age of diagnosis of 67years. There is a slight excess of male patients, and incidence seems to increase with age. The prevalence of renal failure, anaemia and hypercalcaemia at diagnosis was computed to be at 26%, 44% and 18%, respectively, in patients with MM. According to the literature, IgE MM is more aggressive and associated with poorer survival. Nonetheless, cases that are prolonged have also been described.
